review_candidates.description: Job Type Full-time Description Fermi America is developing the largest next generation private power campus in the United States to serve the compute demand of artificial intelligence. As hyperscale load growth outpaces the capability of the legacy grid, Fermi is delivering behind the meter, utility scale power at a speed and density the incumbent market cannot match. Project Matador, our flagship development in Carson County, Texas, is planned to scale to approximately 17 GW of generation, comprising roughly 11 GW of natural gas, 5.4 GW of nuclear, and 600 MW of solar, supporting millions of square feet of high density data center infrastructure. This is not incremental infrastructure. It is sovereign scale energy development, executed on an owner led delivery model. Position Summary The Construction Manager is Fermi America's owner representative in the field for an assigned construction area on Project Matador, within the Capital Projects organization that holds single point accountability for capital project delivery. The role is accountable for the day to day direction of the contractors executing that area, for the safe and productive delivery of the work, and for the owner interfaces that the contractors depend on to keep work fronts open: engineering deliverables, owner furnished equipment, laydown and logistics, permits, site access, and adjacent scopes. This is a field leadership position. The Construction Manager is on the work daily, knows the status of every active work front without waiting for a report, and holds contractors to the Fermi America standard for safety, quality, schedule, and cost. The role represents the owner in field level commercial matters, including field change identification, documentation of contractor performance, and substantiation of positions that Project Controls, the Project Manager, and the Construction Director take forward. This role sits on the owner side of the table. It is not a contractor coordination position and it is not a support function. The Construction Manager is expected to direct contractors, make field decisions within delegated authority, and defend them with facts. Assigned Areas Fermi America is hiring several Construction Managers at this level. Each will be assigned one of the following areas, with the potential for reassignment as the campus phasing evolves. These seats sit alongside the existing Construction Managers for Power and for Electrical and HV. Power. Reports to the Construction Director, Site. Gas turbine generation blocks including simple cycle and combined cycle units, heat recovery steam generators, cooling systems, fuel gas conditioning, balance of plant, and the offload, laydown, and set of owner furnished major equipment. The current Construction Manager Power directs the Firebird SGT-800 and GE Frame 6B and TM2500 programs. Site Infrastructure. Reports to the Construction Director, Site. Site civil and earthwork, campus roads and drainage, water and wastewater systems, natural gas supply and metering infrastructure, temporary facilities, laydown yards, fencing and security infrastructure, and campus utilities serving generation and data center parcels. Data Centers. Reports to the Construction Director, Data Centers. Assigned by tenant campus: data center shell, core, and site works, data center substations and campus electrical interfaces, and field management of the tenant design build contractor, working with the Project Manager Data Centers for that tenant. Key Responsibilities Field Execution and Contractor Direction Direct the EPC and construction contractors executing the assigned area as the owner's field representative, including daily coordination, work front planning, and resolution of field issues. Own the construction execution plan for the assigned area, including work sequencing, area logistics, crane and heavy haul planning, temporary facilities, and interfaces with adjacent areas. Maintain a current, first hand understanding of progress, manpower, equipment, and constraints on every active work front and report it accurately to the Construction Director and the Project Manager. Identify constraints early and clear them through the owner organization: engineering, procurement, permits, access, and owner furnished equipment. Lead constructability reviews on assigned scope and drive contractor adoption of the resulting actions. Safety and Environmental Set and enforce the Fermi America safety standard on the assigned area, holding contractors to Fermi requirements and applicable OSHA regulation without exception. Participate in job safety analysis reviews, pre task planning, incident investigation, and corrective action closeout in coordination with the HSSE Area Manager. Ensure construction activities comply with site environmental permit conditions and stormwater controls in coordination with HSSE and Permitting. Quality Ensure work is executed to the issued for construction drawings and specifications and to the contractor's approved inspection and test plans. Coordinate with the QA/QC Area Manager on witness and hold points, nonconformance reporting, and closeout of quality findings. Drive systems completion readiness, including punch list management, mechanical completion walkdowns, and turnover package assembly in coordination with the Commissioning Manager and the Construction Completions Manager. Owner Furnished Equipment and Logistics Manage the receipt, offload, laydown, preservation, and issue of owner furnished equipment and materials within the assigned area, including transfer of care, custody, and control to the installing contractor. Coordinate with the Materials Manager, Procurement, and Logistics on delivery sequencing, heavy haul routing, site receiving, and damage inspection so deliveries align with the installation schedule. Maintain laydown yard organization, material inventory custody, and warehouse interfaces for the assigned area. Schedule, Cost, and Commercial Support Review and validate contractor progress reporting, schedule updates, and look ahead plans against field reality; challenge reported percent complete where it is not supported. Identify field changes, trends, and potential claims as they arise; document them contemporaneously and provide the EPC Project Controls team with the factual record required for change management. Support the Construction Director, the Project Manager, and the Commercial Manager with field substantiation for change order evaluation, backcharges, and dispute positions. Interfaces and Coordination Own the construction interfaces between the assigned area and adjacent scopes, including generation, high voltage electrical, gas and water infrastructure, and data center parcels, so that interface points are defined, scheduled, and closed. Participate in weekly construction coordination meetings and provide the assigned area input to the Fermi America weekly operations reporting cycle. Build constructive, disciplined working relationships with contractor site leadership while protecting the owner position. Buscamos un perfil técnico de infraestructura, con experiencia práctica en la administración de sistemas Linux y plataformas OpenShift , capaz de gestionar el ciclo de vida de los clústeres y los componentes necesarios para el despliegue y operación de aplicaciones contenerizadas. La persona seleccionada participará en la administración diaria de la plataforma, la resolución de incidencias de nivel avanzado, el soporte a los procesos de despliegue, la gestión de recursos y cargas de trabajo y la evolución controlada de la infraestructura. El modelo de referencia utilizado por Inetum contempla OpenShift como una torre tecnológica especializada N2, encargada de las actuaciones complejas, el soporte a cambios, los despliegues, la resolución de incidencias y la transferencia de conocimiento hacia los niveles iniciales de operación. Funciones y responsabilidades Las Principales Responsabilidades Serán Administración de sistemas Linux Administración avanzada de servidores Linux, principalmente Red Hat Enterprise Linux o distribuciones equivalentes. Instalación, configuración, actualización, parcheado y mantenimiento de sistemas. Diagnóstico y resolución de incidencias de sistema operativo, rendimiento, comunicaciones, almacenamiento y servicios. Administración mediante línea de comandos y automatización de tareas utilizando Bash, Shell o Ansible. Revisión de logs, procesos, servicios, consumo de recursos y comportamiento del sistema. Aplicación de procedimientos de hardening y buenas prácticas de administración. Administración de OpenShift Administración y soporte de clústeres Red Hat OpenShift. Gestión de nodos de control, nodos worker, nodos de infraestructura y recursos asociados. Administración del ciclo de vida de los clústeres, incluyendo actualizaciones, parcheado y revisión de compatibilidades. Gestión de proyectos, namespaces, usuarios, grupos, roles y permisos mediante RBAC. Administración de operadores y componentes propios del ecosistema OpenShift. Gestión de almacenamiento persistente, volúmenes, Storage Classes y Persistent Volume Claims. Configuración y administración de rutas, servicios, ingress, balanceo y conectividad de los clústeres. Gestión de taints, tolerations, affinities, quotas, limits y políticas de asignación de recursos. Revisión del estado, capacidad, disponibilidad y rendimiento de los clústeres. Resolución de incidencias de nivel N2 y N3 relacionadas con OpenShift y Kubernetes. La experiencia utilizada internamente como referencia para este tipo de perfil incluye administración de clústeres OpenShift 4.x, actualizaciones de versión, soporte N3, administración de nodos, OpenShift Logging, Nexus, Prometheus, HAProxy, almacenamiento persistente y automatización con Ansible. Gestión de despliegues y cargas de trabajo Soporte técnico a los equipos responsables del despliegue de aplicaciones. Gestión y diagnóstico de pods, deployments, replicasets, statefulsets, daemonsets, jobs y cronjobs. Análisis de fallos de arranque, reinicios, problemas de scheduling y consumo anómalo de recursos. Gestión de configuraciones, secretos, imágenes y repositorios de contenedores. Revisión y aplicación de manifiestos YAML, Helm Charts u otros mecanismos de despliegue utilizados en la plataforma. Soporte a los procesos de promoción entre los distintos entornos. Validación técnica de los despliegues y resolución de incidencias asociadas a la infraestructura. Coordinación con equipos de aplicaciones, comunicaciones, almacenamiento, seguridad y fabricantes. En los servicios actuales, la operación de OpenShift incluye soporte a despliegues, revisión de métricas y logs, seguimiento de componentes técnicos, participación en actuaciones evolutivas y coordinación con los equipos que intervienen en aplicaciones o servicios relacionados. Requisitos Requisitos imprescindibles Experiencia sólida como administrador/a sénior de sistemas Linux. Experiencia práctica y demostrable en administración de Red Hat OpenShift. Como alternativa, se podrán valorar perfiles con experiencia avanzada en Kubernetes, siempre que aporten una base sólida en Linux y capacidad para asumir la administración de OpenShift. Experiencia en administración de clústeres y resolución de incidencias de nivel avanzado. Conocimientos de contenedores, pods, deployments, operadores, almacenamiento persistente, redes y seguridad de acceso. Experiencia en el uso de YAML y herramientas de línea de comandos como oc y kubectl. Conocimiento de monitorización, gestión de logs y análisis de rendimiento. Capacidad para documentar procedimientos, configuraciones y actuaciones. Autonomía técnica, orientación a la operación y capacidad para trabajar coordinadamente con distintos equipos. Conocimientos valorables Red Hat Enterprise Linux. Ansible y AWX. Docker o Podman. Helm y Kustomize. Prometheus y Grafana. OpenShift Logging, ELK o Kibana.
